# Write: Synthetic practice

Create a folder named `reports/` in the main project folder, then create `reports/synthetic-report.qmd`. The entire folder is ignored by Git; learner reports are not book chapters.

Copy this starter and replace the bracketed text with your own checked results:

````markdown
---
title: "Synthetic practice: analysis report"
format: html
---

## Question and data
[Question, organism, source, counts technology, cells, samples and donor limitations.]

## Methods
[Input checks, QC thresholds, retained cells, normalization, selected genes, PCA and software versions.]

## Results
[Describe actual observations with values.]

![Cell quality](../results/synthetic/qc.png)

![Exploratory PCA](../results/synthetic/pca.png)

## Independent verification
[Cell ID, manual calculation, saved value and verifier result.]

## Interpretation and limitations
[What the data support; technical alternatives; what is not established.]

## AI use
[What AI helped with and how you checked its response.]

## Next step
[One justified follow-up.]
````

Also create `reports/_quarto.yml` with the following contents so learner reports have their own Quarto project:

```yaml
project:
  type: default
  output-dir: .
```

In the terminal, enter `reports/` and render there:

```bash
cd reports
quarto render synthetic-report.qmd
cd ..
```

The HTML stays in `reports/`. Read it and confirm both figures display. If you share the report, inspect it for private metadata first.
